data.long_meaning: Ayanna is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Ayus’ meaning 'life'. The name Ayanna is a feminine form of Ayu, which is a Sanskrit name for the Hindu god of life. The name Ayanna signifies the divine and celestial aspect of life. The name is radiant and full of grace. The name Ayanna carries the meaning “Divine, Celestial, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ayanna usually hope their child will grow to embody divine, celestial, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Ayanna was a queen of the Satavahana dynasty, ruling from around 130-100 BCE. She is known for her military campaigns against the Shakas and the Sakas in the west and the Andhras in the south. Her inscriptions reveal that she was a generous patron of Buddhism.
historical_references.context: Satavahana Dynasty, Military Campaigns against Shakas, Sakas and Andhras, Generous Patron of Buddhism

historical_references.reference: Ayanna, also known as Ayangama, was a legendary queen of the Chalukya dynasty in the 7th century CE. She is revered as a goddess in Hinduism, and her shrine at Vadabhate in Karnataka state attracts numerous pilgrims. According to legend, she was a fierce warrior and defeated an invading army single-handedly.
historical_references.context: Chalukya Dynasty, Revered as a Goddess, Legendary Fighter
